view.stem: 不同的两点 $M,H$ 关于直线 $l$ 对称，$P$ 不在 $l$ 上。分别考虑 $P$ 位于 $M$ 所在半平面、$H$ 所在半平面这两种情形，并确定可以作出的所有满足 $OM=OH$ 的点 $O$。哪一项完整说明正确？

options.text: $P$ 在 $M$ 一侧时 $PM\gt PH$，在 $H$ 一侧时 $PM\lt PH$；$O$ 可取直线 $l$ 上的任意点。
$P$ 在 $M$ 一侧时 $PM\lt PH$，在 $H$ 一侧时 $PM\gt PH$；$O$ 可取直线 $l$ 上的任意点。
$P$ 在 $M$ 一侧时 $PM\lt PH$，在 $H$ 一侧时 $PM\gt PH$；$O$ 只能取线段 $MH$ 的中点。

intent.task: Compare the two distances in both possible off-axis half-planes and determine the complete equidistant locus from which O may be constructed.
intent.source_solution: With l:x=0,M=(-a,0),H=(a,0),a>0 and P=(x,y),x!=0,PM^2-PH^2=4ax. Thus P on M's side gives PM<PH and on H's side gives PM>PH. OM=OH iff O is on the entire l. Any point on l works,not only its intersection with MH. Specifying distinct reflected endpoints makes the ordinary nondegenerate construction explicit;no order of P's distances is guessed.
intent.unit_reason: One complete case-and-locus response preserves both distance comparisons and the possible positions of the constructed O;the source's unspecified side is resolved by casework rather than fixed artificially.
limitations: Does not demonstrate drawing l,constructing the reflected pair,choosing off-axis P or actually marking O.

rationales.derivation: Reverse the interpretation of a half-plane:for x<0 take4ax to imply PM>PH instead of PM<PH,and reverse the other side likewise. Retain the correct whole-axis locus. For a=1,P=(-2,0),actual PM=1,PH=3 contradict A.
rationales.misconception: Associate the nearer half-plane with the farther reflected point,thus reversing both distance inequalities.

rationales.derivation: PM^2-PH^2=4ax and nonnegative distances give the two stated strict inequalities;the same difference is0 exactly when x=0,so every and only axis point can be O.

Solve OM=OH only on the joining segment MH,obtaining its midpoint,and incorrectly declare that restricted solution the entire plane locus. With M=(-1,0),H=(1,0),O=(0,2),OM=OH=sqrt(5) although O is not the midpoint.
rationales.misconception: Restrict an equidistance locus to the original joining segment and omit every other point on its perpendicular bisector.

view.stem: 取不同的两点 $P,N$，并另外画非零线段 $MK$；分别用圆规和直尺作这两对端点的对称轴。下面用 $S,T$ 表示其中任一对端点。哪种作法对两对端点都能得到所需的整条对称轴？

options.text: 以 $S,T$ 为圆心，均用半径 $ST/2$ 画圆；把两个圆的交点记为 $U,V$，作直线 $UV$。

intent.task: Recognize a compass-and-straightedge construction valid for both distinct P,N and the endpoints of a drawn nonzero MK segment,including the strict radius condition and full axis.
intent.source_solution: For S!=T,d=ST>0,two circles of equal radius r>d/2 have two distinct intersections U,V. Both satisfy US=UT and VS=VT;the full UV is the perpendicular bisector and exchanges S,T under reflection. r=d/2 has only one intersection. Unequal radii give a radical axis with a nonzero squared-distance difference,not the equidistant locus.
intent.unit_reason: The two sources ask the same generic endpoint-pair construction;one shared method response avoids duplicate questions while retaining the extra source requirement to draw the closed MK segment.
limitations: Does not demonstrate physically carrying out either compass-and-straightedge construction.
Does not demonstrate drawing the nonzero closed segment MK with its endpoints.

rationales.derivation: Choose the radius exactly d/2 instead of strictly greater. The two circles are externally tangent at the midpoint,so U=V and no unique joining line UV exists. Two distinct points needed to construct the axis have not been obtained.

rationales.derivation: Use unequal radii rS,rT. Their intersection points satisfy XS^2-XT^2=rS^2-rT^2!=0,so their common chord line is not the zero-difference perpendicular bisector. Example S=(-1,0),T=(1,0),rS=2,rT=sqrt(2) gives intersection line x=1/2,not x=0.
rationales.misconception: Assume two-circle intersections are equidistant from the centers even when the compass radii differ.

rationales.derivation: Equal r>d/2 yields two distinct equidistant points;the unique full line through them is the entire perpendicular-bisector locus. The construction depends only on the two distinct endpoints and works for both named pairs.

rationales.derivation: For the first pair the segment slope is3,so the midpoint perpendicular has slope-1/3. For the second the segment slope is-1,so its midpoint perpendicular has slope1 and y=x. Squared-distance equalities confirm both entire loci.

Take the reciprocal of the joining slope without negating it. Slope3 becomes1/3 through(0,0),giving x-3y=0;slope-1 remains-1 through(-3,-3),giving x+y=-6. Each line passes through its midpoint but is not the required perpendicular.
rationales.misconception: Use the reciprocal slope instead of the negative reciprocal for a perpendicular line.

rationales.derivation: Compute the correct midpoints but always draw a vertical line through them,producing x=0 and x=-3. (0,1) on the first proposed axis has distances sqrt(5),sqrt(17) to A,B;(-3,0) on the second has squared distances17 and5 to C,D.

intent.task: Form the common-unit-price model for each of two independent purchases,include both item counts,and remove each separately priced item before dividing.
intent.source_solution: For p,q in cents,the separate models are(6+4)p+13=73 and(7+6)q+35=61. Thus p=60/10=6 cents,q=26/13=2 cents,both positive;source story3/4 are retained in the separate thought-number response.
intent.unit_reason: The two purchases share the complete count-times-common-price plus fixed-item model. A full ordered price pair retains both independent stories without conflating their price variables.
limitations: Does not demonstrate independently formulating and writing either price equation or complete word-problem solution.

rationales.derivation: Subtract the fixed item correctly but divide only by the first named type's count,ignoring4 small breads and6 ruled books. Prices become(73-13)/6=10 and(61-35)/7=26/7 cents. Their true full purchase costs would exceed the stated totals.
rationales.misconception: Count only one of the two equal-price item types when finding a common unit price.

rationales.derivation: Count10 equal-price breads and13 equal-price notebooks;remove13 and35 cents respectively from the bills. The remaining60 and26 cents give6 and2 cents per item.

intent.task: Preserve both complete ordered operation chains and distinguish the original thought numbers from intermediate sums/differences.
intent.source_solution: Separate real unknowns x,z satisfy9(x+5)+x-25=200 and6(z-3)-z+48=90. Reduction gives10x+20=200,x=18 and5z+30=90,z=12. Complete sequences18,23,207,225,200 and12,9,54,42,90 verify every operation.
intent.unit_reason: One complete original-number pair compares two related but independent operation-chain models;these are mathematically distinct from the two price models and thus form their own response unit.
limitations: Does not demonstrate independently translating both word chains into equations or writing the complete transformations.

rationales.derivation: Solve to the true original18,12 but report the values after the first operation:18+5=23 and12-3=9. These are intermediate values,not the original numbers. Starting with23 yields250 instead of200;starting with9 yields75 instead of90.
rationales.misconception: Report the first shifted intermediate value instead of the original unknown.

rationales.derivation: Distribute each multiplier only to the variable,not the bracket constant. The altered chains9x+5+x-25=200 and6z-3-z+48=90 become10x-20=200 and5z+45=90,yielding22 and9.

view.stem: 如图，从外面的正方形割去四个合同的角三角形。哪一段论证能完整证明剩下的四边形 $ABCD$ 是正方形？

options.text: 四个三角形的斜边合同，所以 $AB=BC=CD=DA$，$ABCD$ 是菱形；菱形的每个内角都是直角，因此它是正方形。
四条斜边合同，所以四边相等。每个角三角形的两锐角 $\alpha+\beta=90^\circ$；依图中的循环排列，$ABCD$ 每个内角为 $180^\circ-(\alpha+\beta)=90^\circ$，故为正方形。
四个角三角形合同，所以每个三角形的两锐角相等，均为 $45^\circ$。四条斜边合同，剩余四边形每角均为 $180^\circ-45^\circ-45^\circ=90^\circ$，故为正方形。

intent.task: Judge a complete proof of both equal sides and right angles from the four congruent corner triangles in their actual placement;do not replace the proof with the conclusion alone.
intent.source_solution: All inner sides are corresponding hypotenuses,so they are equal. The actual cyclic placement brings complementary acute angles alpha,beta beside a straight outer side at each inner vertex,giving interior angle180-(alpha+beta)=90 degrees. Thus ABCD is a square. Equal sides alone give only a rhombus;congruence of different triangles does not make the two acute angles inside one triangle equal.
intent.unit_reason: One full proof-selection response retains both essential inferences rather than offering only a shape name or one minor equal-side claim.
limitations: Does not demonstrate independently discovering and writing the complete two-part proof.

figure_observations.observation: Opened the full640x512 actual SVG rendering,including bottom outer edge/A label and rightmost B. C is on the top,D on the left;all four closed edges and four cyclic corner triangles are visible. Graphic corner legs104 and312 verify the triangles are not isosceles. Adjacent inner side vectors have dot product0 and equal lengths. A non-square rhombus with60/120 degree angles disproves that inference. The actual final conclusion is true,but A does not prove it from the given facts.
rationales.misconception: Upgrade four equal sides to four right angles by falsely identifying all rhombi as squares.

rationales.derivation: Congruence proves equal hypotenuses. Every removed corner is a right triangle with complementary alpha,beta,and the actual successive quarter-turn placement puts one of each beside a straight side at every inner vertex. The four interior angles are90 degrees,completing the square criterion.

Turn equality of corresponding angles across the four congruent triangles into equality of the two distinct acute angles within each triangle. This wrongly sets alpha=beta=45. Actual graphic legs104 and312 have unequal lengths,so the two acute angles are unequal. The90-degree interior calculation rests on a false premise despite its true final conclusion.
rationales.misconception: Confuse congruence between triangles with isoscelesness of each triangle,and impose equal acute angles without justification.
